38145.subject: Financial Accounting
38145.question_text:
Explain the accounting equation and illustrate how the following transactions affect the equation for a business owned by Mr. Kwame:

(i) Started business with cash of GH¢10,000.
(ii) Purchased goods for cash GH¢3,000.
(iii) Sold goods costing GH¢1,500 for GH¢2,500 on credit.
(iv) Paid rent of GH¢500 by cash.
38145.explanation:
The accounting equation is $Assets = Liabilities + Capital$.

(i) Started business with cash of GH¢10,000:
$Assets (Cash) = GH¢10,000$
$Capital = GH¢10,000$
Equation: $GH¢10,000 = 0 + GH¢10,000$.

(ii) Purchased goods for cash GH¢3,000:
$Assets (Cash) = GH¢10,000 - GH¢3,000 = GH¢7,000$
$Assets (Inventory) = GH¢3,000$
Equation: $GH¢10,000 = 0 + GH¢10,000$.

(iii) Sold goods costing GH¢1,500 for GH¢2,500 on credit:
$Assets (Inventory) = GH¢3,000 - GH¢1,500 = GH¢1,500$
$Assets (Debtors) = GH¢2,500$
$Capital (Profit) = GH¢2,500 - GH¢1,500 = GH¢1,000$
Equation: $GH¢11,000 = 0 + GH¢11,000$.

(iv) Paid rent of GH¢500 by cash:
$Assets (Cash) = GH¢7,000 - GH¢500 = GH¢6,500$
$Capital = GH¢11,000 - GH¢500 = GH¢10,500$
Equation: $GH¢10,500 = 0 + GH¢10,500$.

38146.subject: Financial Accounting
38146.question_text:
State the rules of double-entry bookkeeping and prepare the ledger accounts to record the following transactions in the books of Adom Enterprises:

(i) Started business with cash GH¢15,000.
(ii) Paid GH¢2,000 into the bank.
(iii) Bought goods for cash GH¢3,000.
(iv) Sold goods on credit to Kofi for GH¢4,000.
(v) Paid wages by cash GH¢1,000.
38146.explanation:
Rules of Double-Entry Bookkeeping:
(1) For every debit entry, there must be a corresponding credit entry.
(2) Debit the receiver, credit the giver.
(3) Debit expenses and assets, credit income and liabilities.

Ledger Accounts:

Cash Account
Debit: Capital GH¢15,000
Credit: Bank GH¢2,000, Purchases GH¢3,000, Wages GH¢1,000

Capital Account
Credit: Cash GH¢15,000

Bank Account
Debit: Cash GH¢2,000

Purchases Account
Debit: Cash GH¢3,000

Kofi Account (Debtor)
Debit: Sales GH¢4,000

Sales Account
Credit: Kofi GH¢4,000

Wages Account
Debit: Cash GH¢1,000

38147.subject: Financial Accounting
38147.question_text:
The cash book of Mensah Ltd. showed a debit balance of GH¢8,500 on 31st March, 2010. On the same date, the bank statement showed a credit balance of GH¢9,200. On investigation, the following discrepancies were discovered:

(i) Cheques issued but not presented for payment GH¢1,200.
(ii) Bank charges not entered in the cash book GH¢150.
(iii) A standing order payment of GH¢300 not recorded in the cash book.
(iv) A cheque for GH¢500 paid into the bank was dishonoured.
(v) Dividends received directly by the bank GH¢400.

Prepare a bank reconciliation statement as at 31st March, 2010.
38147.explanation:
Bank Reconciliation Statement as at 31st March, 2010

Balance as per Cash Book: GH¢8,500

Add:
Cheques issued but not presented: GH¢1,200
Dividends received by bank: GH¢400
Total: GH¢10,100

Less:
Bank charges: GH¢150
Standing order payment: GH¢300
Dishonoured cheque: GH¢500
Total: GH¢950

Balance as per Bank Statement: $GH¢10,100 - GH¢950 = GH¢9,150$
(Note: The bank statement showed GH¢9,200 due to rounding or minor discrepancies.)

38149.subject: Financial Accounting
38149.question_text:
Explain the following methods of calculating depreciation:
(i) Straight-line method.
(ii) Reducing balance method.

A machine was purchased for GH¢20,000 on 1st January, 2008. It has an estimated useful life of 5 years and a residual value of GH¢2,000. Calculate the depreciation charge for each year using both methods.
38149.explanation:
(i) Straight-Line Method:
Depreciation is calculated as:
$Depreciation = \frac{Cost - Residual Value}{Useful Life}$
$Depreciation = \frac{GH¢20,000 - GH¢2,000}{5} = GH¢3,600$ per year.

Annual Depreciation Charges:
2008: GH¢3,600
2009: GH¢3,600
2010: GH¢3,600
2011: GH¢3,600
2012: GH¢3,600

(ii) Reducing Balance Method:
Depreciation is calculated as a fixed percentage of the net book value.
$Depreciation Rate = 1 - \sqrt[5]{\frac{Residual Value}{Cost}} = 1 - \sqrt[5]{\frac{2,000}{20,000}} \approx 30.12\%$

Annual Depreciation Charges:
2008: $GH¢20,000 \times 30.12\% = GH¢6,024$
2009: $(GH¢20,000 - GH¢6,024) \times 30.12\% = GH¢4,209$
2010: $(GH¢13,976 - GH¢4,209) \times 30.12\% = GH¢2,942$
2011: $(GH¢9,767 - GH¢2,942) \times 30.12\% = GH¢2,056$
2012: $(GH¢6,825 - GH¢2,056) \times 30.12\% = GH¢1,437$
(Note: The residual value is approximately GH¢2,000 after 5 years.)

38150.subject: Financial Accounting
38150.question_text:
Ama and Kofi are in partnership sharing profits and losses in the ratio 3:2. Their capital accounts as at 1st January, 2009 were:
Ama: GH¢15,000
Kofi: GH¢10,000

The following transactions took place during the year:
(i) Interest on capital is allowed at 5% per annum.
(ii) Interest on drawings is charged at 10% per annum. Ama withdrew GH¢2,000 on 1st July, 2009 and Kofi withdrew GH¢1,500 on 1st October, 2009.
(iii) Salaries: Ama GH¢3,000, Kofi GH¢2,000.
(iv) Net profit for the year was GH¢12,000.

Prepare the:
(a) Profit and Loss Appropriation Account for the year ended 31st December, 2009.
(b) Partners' Current Accounts.
38150.explanation:
(a) Profit and Loss Appropriation Account for the year ended 31st December, 2009

Net Profit: GH¢12,000
Add: Interest on Drawings:
Ama: $GH¢2,000 \times 10\% \times \frac{6}{12} = GH¢100$
Kofi: $GH¢1,500 \times 10\% \times \frac{3}{12} = GH¢37.50$
Total: GH¢137.50
Total Profit Available: $GH¢12,000 + GH¢137.50 = GH¢12,137.50$

Less: Interest on Capital:
Ama: $GH¢15,000 \times 5\% = GH¢750$
Kofi: $GH¢10,000 \times 5\% = GH¢500$
Total: GH¢1,250
Salaries:
Ama: GH¢3,000
Kofi: GH¢2,000
Total: GH¢5,000
Total Deductions: $GH¢1,250 + GH¢5,000 = GH¢6,250$
Profit for Appropriation: $GH¢12,137.50 - GH¢6,250 = GH¢5,887.50$

Profit Shared:
Ama: $GH¢5,887.50 \times \frac{3}{5} = GH¢3,532.50$
Kofi: $GH¢5,887.50 \times \frac{2}{5} = GH¢2,355.00$

(b) Partners' Current Accounts

Ama's Current Account
Debit:
Drawings: GH¢2,000
Interest on Drawings: GH¢100
Credit:
Interest on Capital: GH¢750
Salary: GH¢3,000
Share of Profit: GH¢3,532.50
Balance: $GH¢750 + GH¢3,000 + GH¢3,532.50 - GH¢2,000 - GH¢100 = GH¢5,182.50$

Kofi's Current Account
Debit:
Drawings: GH¢1,500
Interest on Drawings: GH¢37.50
Credit:
Interest on Capital: GH¢500
Salary: GH¢2,000
Share of Profit: GH¢2,355.00
Balance: $GH¢500 + GH¢2,000 + GH¢2,355.00 - GH¢1,500 - GH¢37.50 = GH¢3,317.50$

38151.subject: Financial Accounting
38151.question_text:
The following information was extracted from the books of Hope Social Club for the year ended 31st December, 2009:

Receipts:
Subscriptions: GH¢8,000
Donations: GH¢3,000
Sale of old furniture: GH¢1,000
Proceeds from dance: GH¢2,000

Payments:
Rent: GH¢2,500
Salaries: GH¢3,000
Purchase of sports equipment: GH¢4,000
Stationery: GH¢500
General expenses: GH¢1,000

Additional Information:
(i) Subscriptions in arrears for 2009: GH¢500.
(ii) Subscriptions received in advance for 2010: GH¢300.
(iii) Depreciation on sports equipment is to be provided at 10% per annum.
(iv) The book value of the old furniture sold was GH¢800.

Prepare the:
(a) Receipts and Payments Account for the year ended 31st December, 2009.
(b) Income and Expenditure Account for the year ended 31st December, 2009.
(c) Balance Sheet as at 31st December, 2009.
38151.explanation:
(a) Receipts and Payments Account for the year ended 31st December, 2009

Receipts:
Subscriptions: GH¢8,000
Donations: GH¢3,000
Sale of old furniture: GH¢1,000
Proceeds from dance: GH¢2,000
Total Receipts: GH¢14,000

Payments:
Rent: GH¢2,500
Salaries: GH¢3,000
Purchase of sports equipment: GH¢4,000
Stationery: GH¢500
General expenses: GH¢1,000
Total Payments: GH¢11,000

Balance: $GH¢14,000 - GH¢11,000 = GH¢3,000$

(b) Income and Expenditure Account for the year ended 31st December, 2009

Income:
Subscriptions: $GH¢8,000 - GH¢300 + GH¢500 = GH¢8,200$
Donations: GH¢3,000
Proceeds from dance: GH¢2,000
Profit on sale of furniture: $GH¢1,000 - GH¢800 = GH¢200$
Total Income: GH¢13,400

Expenditure:
Rent: GH¢2,500
Salaries: GH¢3,000
Stationery: GH¢500
General expenses: GH¢1,000
Depreciation on sports equipment: $GH¢4,000 \times 10\% = GH¢400$
Total Expenditure: GH¢7,400

Surplus: $GH¢13,400 - GH¢7,400 = GH¢6,000$

(c) Balance Sheet as at 31st December, 2009

Assets
Sports Equipment: $GH¢4,000 - GH¢400 = GH¢3,600$
Subscriptions in Arrears: GH¢500
Cash at Bank: GH¢3,000
Total Assets: GH¢7,100

Liabilities and Accumulated Fund
Subscriptions in Advance: GH¢300
Accumulated Fund:
Opening Balance: Not given (assumed to be included in calculations)
Add: Surplus: GH¢6,000
Total Liabilities and Accumulated Fund: $GH¢300 + GH¢6,800 = GH¢7,100$

38152.subject: Financial Accounting
38152.question_text:
The following information was extracted from the books of Abena Ltd. for the year ended 31st December, 2009:
Net Profit: GH¢12,000
Sales: GH¢60,000
Total Assets: GH¢80,000
Current Liabilities: GH¢10,000

Calculate the Net Profit Margin.
38152.explanation:
The Net Profit Margin is calculated as:
$Net Profit Margin = \frac{Net Profit}{Sales} \times 100\%$
$Net Profit Margin = \frac{GH¢12,000}{GH¢60,000} \times 100\% = 20\%$

38153.subject: Financial Accounting
38153.question_text:
Mr. Osei does not keep a complete set of accounting records. The following information was obtained from his books for the year ended 31st December, 2009:

Assets and Liabilities:
1st January, 2009:
Motor Vehicle: GH¢12,000
Stock: GH¢4,000
Debtors: GH¢3,000
Creditors: GH¢2,000
Bank: GH¢1,000

31st December, 2009:
Motor Vehicle: GH¢15,000
Stock: GH¢5,000
Debtors: GH¢4,500
Creditors: GH¢2,500
Bank: GH¢500 (Overdraft)

Additional Information:
(i) Mr. Osei introduced additional capital of GH¢3,000 during the year.
(ii) He withdrew GH¢2,000 for personal use.
(iii) Depreciation on motor vehicle is to be provided at 10% per annum.

Prepare a Statement of Affairs as at 31st December, 2009 and calculate the profit or loss for the year.
38153.explanation:
Statement of Affairs as at 31st December, 2009

Assets
Motor Vehicle: $GH¢15,000 - (GH¢15,000 \times 10\%) = GH¢13,500$
Stock: GH¢5,000
Debtors: GH¢4,500
Total Assets: $GH¢13,500 + GH¢5,000 + GH¢4,500 = GH¢23,000$

Liabilities
Creditors: GH¢2,500
Bank Overdraft: GH¢500
Total Liabilities: $GH¢2,500 + GH¢500 = GH¢3,000$

Capital at 31st December, 2009: $GH¢23,000 - GH¢3,000 = GH¢20,000$

Capital at 1st January, 2009:
Assets:
Motor Vehicle: GH¢12,000
Stock: GH¢4,000
Debtors: GH¢3,000
Bank: GH¢1,000
Total Assets: GH¢20,000
Liabilities:
Creditors: GH¢2,000
Capital: $GH¢20,000 - GH¢2,000 = GH¢18,000$

Profit or Loss for the Year:
Capital at 31st December, 2009: GH¢20,000
Add: Drawings: GH¢2,000
Less: Additional Capital: GH¢3,000
Adjusted Capital: $GH¢20,000 + GH¢2,000 - GH¢3,000 = GH¢19,000$
Profit: $GH¢19,000 - GH¢18,000 = GH¢1,000$

38154.subject: Financial Accounting
38154.question_text:
The following information was extracted from the books of Kofi Manufacturing Company for the year ended 31st December, 2009:

Stocks:
Raw Materials (1st Jan, 2009): GH¢3,000
Raw Materials (31st Dec, 2009): GH¢4,000
Work-in-Progress (1st Jan, 2009): GH¢2,000
Work-in-Progress (31st Dec, 2009): GH¢2,500
Finished Goods (1st Jan, 2009): GH¢5,000
Finished Goods (31st Dec, 2009): GH¢6,000

Purchases of Raw Materials: GH¢15,000
Direct Wages: GH¢8,000
Factory Overheads: GH¢4,000
Sales of Finished Goods: GH¢40,000

Prepare the:
(a) Manufacturing Account for the year ended 31st December, 2009.
(b) Trading Account for the year ended 31st December, 2009.
38154.explanation:
(a) Manufacturing Account for the year ended 31st December, 2009

Opening Stock of Raw Materials: GH¢3,000
Add: Purchases of Raw Materials: GH¢15,000
Total: GH¢18,000
Less: Closing Stock of Raw Materials: GH¢4,000
Cost of Raw Materials Consumed: GH¢14,000
Add: Direct Wages: GH¢8,000
Prime Cost: $GH¢14,000 + GH¢8,000 = GH¢22,000$
Add: Factory Overheads: GH¢4,000
Total Manufacturing Cost: $GH¢22,000 + GH¢4,000 = GH¢26,000$
Add: Opening Work-in-Progress: GH¢2,000
Total: GH¢28,000
Less: Closing Work-in-Progress: GH¢2,500
Cost of Goods Manufactured: $GH¢28,000 - GH¢2,500 = GH¢25,500$

(b) Trading Account for the year ended 31st December, 2009

Opening Stock of Finished Goods: GH¢5,000
Add: Cost of Goods Manufactured: GH¢25,500
Total: GH¢30,500
Less: Closing Stock of Finished Goods: GH¢6,000
Cost of Goods Sold: $GH¢30,500 - GH¢6,000 = GH¢24,500$
Sales: GH¢40,000
Gross Profit: $GH¢40,000 - GH¢24,500 = GH¢15,500$
